objective:
【研究命题·纯机器学习/数学】

解空间刚性 = 满足全部解析约束的函数集合的维数：低维/唯一 = 刚，高维/连续族 = 胖。

核心问题：小型前馈网络的“泛化行为”能否作为 bootstrap 解空间刚性的探针？
令 w = 约束样本数，N_c(w) = 在未参与训练的留出约束点上取得“零违规”所需的最小网络容量（用隐藏层宽度度量）。

【唯一硬性口径（不可更改，其余全由你决定）】
- 零违规 = 留出约束点上的最大绝对误差 ≤ 1e-3。
- 刚性 = 扫描范围内存在较小的有限 N_c（且 N_c 不随 w 增长）；胖 = 扫描上限内任何宽度都达不到零违规（N_c 不可达）。判别是二值的。
- 所有报告数值必须是有限数（禁止 inf/nan/None）。
- 研究对象只能是小型前馈网络本身。严禁把本命题替换或“换名归约”为材料/化学/玻璃/合金/离子导电等任何物理体系，也不要用别的领域类比回答。

【实验的族、样本、扫描、脚本如何设计，以及如何证明“刚性可达”，由你自己决定并给出理由。】

所有结论必须来自真实运行的可复现数值实验：给出扫描设置、训练与留出误差数值、以及 N_c(w) 的数值与趋势。

input_params.description: Design a numerical experiment to test if small feedforward networks can probe solution space rigidity. Define a class of analytic constraints (e.g., polynomial or trigonometric functions with known solution properties), vary the number of constraints w, and scan hidden layer widths N to find N_c(w) — the minimum width achieving zero violation (max abs error ≤ 1e-3) on held-out test points. Train small MLPs (1–2 hidden layers, activation=ReLU) on w constraints sampled from the target function, evaluate on a dense grid of test points, record N_c(w), and assess whether N_c remains bounded (rigid) or diverges (fat) as w increases. Use 3–5 random seeds per (w,N) for robustness.
input_params.expected_prediction: N_c(w) will remain small and bounded (e.g., N_c ≤ 16) for w up to ~20, indicating rigidity; if no width achieves zero violation within scan range (e.g., N ≤ 128), then fat. Expected trend: flat or sublinear N_c(w) if rigid, superlinear or divergent if fat.

prediction_inputs.label: training_samples
prediction_inputs.value: w points sampled from target function

input_params.description: Design and run a numerical experiment to test the hypothesis that the minimal width N_c(w) for zero violation on out-of-sample points is bounded by a constant (≤ d+1) independent of sample size w. We will: (1) construct a low-degree algebraic constraint manifold of known dimension d (e.g., a 2D polynomial surface in R^3); (2) sample w points from w=5 to 40; (3) train small feedforward networks of varying width N to interpolate training points; (4) measure out-of-sample max absolute error on held-out points; (5) determine N_c(w) as the smallest width achieving max error ≤ 1e-3. We will compare against the prediction that N_c(w) remains ≤ d+1 (e.g., ≤3) across all w. This directly tests the algebraic geometry claim about intrinsic dimensionality limiting network capacity.
input_params.expected_prediction: N_c(w) will remain small and bounded (e.g., N_c ≤ d+1 ≈ 3-5) for w up to 40, with out-of-sample error ≤ 1e-3 achieved at fixed width across all w, supporting the "rigid" hypothesis. If error exceeds 1e-3 at all widths for large w, the hypothesis is rejected as "fat".

input_params.description: Systematically scan the capacity parameter space (hidden width N) vs constraint count w to measure N_c(w). For each w, sweep N from a lower bound (e.g., 10) to an upper bound (e.g., 200) until zero-violation is achieved (max absolute error on held-out points ≤ 1e-3). Use a small synthetic function family to generate the bootstrap constraints. Record the minimum N for each w. If N_c plateaus at a finite value as w increases, the hypothesis is supported (rigid); if N_c grows without bound or never reaches zero-violation within the scan range, the hypothesis is rejected (fat).
input_params.expected_prediction: The scan will reveal that N_c(w) remains constant (e.g., N_c ≈ 15-25) for w in the tested range (e.g., w=10 to w=100), indicating a plateau. This confirms the algebraic variety structure hypothesis. If N_c grows linearly with w or fails to converge to zero-violation, the fat hypothesis is supported.

input_params.description: I will design a computational experiment to test the hypothesis that minimal network width N_c(w) grows logarithmically with constraint count w for a gradient-flow-governed solution space. The plan: (1) Define a constrained regression problem with w linear equality constraints sampled from a sharp energy landscape (e.g., high-frequency sinusoidal target with narrow basins). (2) Sweep hidden layer width N ∈ [4, 128] for each w ∈ {10, 20, 50, 100, 200}. (3) For each (w, N) triplet, train a small feedforward network (2 hidden layers, ReLU) on w constraint points and evaluate max absolute error on a held-out test set of w constraints. (4) Determine N_c(w) as the smallest N achieving zero violation (max error ≤ 1e-3). (5) Fit log(w) scaling to N_c(w) and compare against linear/exponential alternatives. This directly tests the numeric claim N_c(w) ∼ log(w) using the specified zero-violation criterion.
input_params.expected_prediction: N_c(w) will show sublinear growth; if the hypothesis holds, log(w) fit will have R² > 0.95 with slope ≈ 1-2 (e.g., N_c(10)≈8, N_c(100)≈16, N_c(200)≈18). If the landscape is too fat, N_c(w) may reach plateau or exceed 128 before zero violation is achieved.
